changes.title: Domestic research costs deductible again under new Section 174A
changes.summary: For tax years beginning after December 31, 2024, domestic research and experimental expenditures are currently deductible under new Section 174A instead of being capitalized and amortized over 5 years under Section 174. Foreign research remains subject to 15-year amortization. Preparers must choose between deducting, electing 10-year amortization under Section 59(e)-style rules, or capitalizing, and small-business taxpayers may apply the change retroactively to 2022-2024 via amended returns or an accounting-method change under Rev. Proc. 2025-28. Expect a changed deduction line treatment and new election statements compared with the 2024 return.
changes.who_is_affected: All corporations with research and experimental expenditures.
changes.effective: Tax years beginning after December 31, 2024; elective retroactivity to 2022 for eligible small-business taxpayers.

excerpt.current: [ILLUSTRATIVE — verify against published instructions] Domestic research or experimental expenditures. For tax years beginning after December 31, 2024, section 174A allows a deduction for domestic research or experimental expenditures paid or incurred during the tax year. Alternatively, the corporation may elect to capitalize and amortize these expenditures over a period of not less than 60 months. Foreign research or experimental expenditures continue to be charged to capital account and amortized over 15 years under section 174.
excerpt.prior: Research and experimental expenditures paid or incurred in tax years beginning after 2021 must be charged to a capital account and amortized ratably over a 5-year period (15-year period for expenditures attributable to foreign research).

changes.title: 100% bonus depreciation permanently restored for property acquired after Jan 19, 2025
changes.summary: The additional first-year depreciation allowance returns to 100% for qualified property acquired after January 19, 2025 and placed in service after that date, replacing the 40% rate that would otherwise have applied for 2025 under the TCJA phase-down. Property acquired on or before January 19, 2025 remains subject to the phase-down percentage. Preparers must track acquisition dates around the January 19, 2025 line and watch for a transitional election to apply the phase-down percentage instead.
changes.who_is_affected: Corporations placing depreciable property in service during 2025.

excerpt.current: [ILLUSTRATIVE — verify against published instructions] Special depreciation allowance. The special depreciation allowance is 100% for qualified property acquired after January 19, 2025, and placed in service after January 19, 2025. For qualified property acquired before January 20, 2025, the allowance remains 40% (60% for certain long production period property and aircraft). See Form 4562 and its instructions.
excerpt.prior: The special depreciation allowance is 60% for qualified property placed in service in 2024.

changes.title: Section 163(j) limitation computed on EBITDA basis again
changes.summary: For tax years beginning after December 31, 2024, adjusted taxable income for the Section 163(j) business interest limitation is once again computed without regard to depreciation, amortization, and depletion (an EBITDA base), permanently reversing the EBIT-based computation that applied for 2022-2024. This generally increases the interest deduction cap. Form 8990 computations and any state decoupling from the change need to be revisited.
changes.who_is_affected: Corporations subject to the business interest expense limitation.

source.section: Limitations on Deductions; Business interest expense

excerpt.current: [ILLUSTRATIVE — verify against published instructions] Business interest expense. For tax years beginning after 2024, adjusted taxable income is computed without regard to any deduction allowable for depreciation, amortization, or depletion. See section 163(j) and Form 8990.
excerpt.prior: For tax years beginning after 2021, adjusted taxable income is computed taking into account deductions for depreciation, amortization, and depletion.

changes.title: Several clean energy credits terminated for 2025-2026
changes.summary: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act terminates a series of clean energy credits that corporations claimed through the general business credit, including the clean vehicle credits for vehicles acquired after September 30, 2025 and the commercial clean vehicle credit on the same date, with energy-property timelines tightened for wind and solar. The 2025 instructions and credit-form lineup reflect terminated or transition-limited credits versus the 2024 lists. Preparers should confirm eligibility dates on each credit form before carrying 2024 positions into 2025.
changes.form: Form 1120 (Schedule J; general business credit forms)
changes.who_is_affected: Corporations claiming clean vehicle or energy credits.
changes.effective: Various dates in 2025-2026 depending on the credit.
